contentBlocks.text: This week you learned all three basic word types and used them to build real sentences. Let's review everything and read a short passage together.

Quick review: nouns (ਨਾਂਵ) name a person, place, or thing (Day 1). Verbs (ਕਿਰਿਆ) tell what something does (Day 2). Adjectives (ਵਿਸ਼ੇਸ਼ਣ) describe a noun, and change form to match masculine or feminine nouns (Day 3-4). Now read this short passage built entirely from words you already know: ਇਹ ਵੱਡਾ ਘਰ ਹੈ। ਕੁੜੀ ਪੜ੍ਹਦੀ ਹੈ। ਕੁੱਤਾ ਖੇਡਦਾ ਹੈ। (This is a big house. The girl reads. The dog plays.)
You just read a real three-sentence passage using only words you learned this week, and reviewed all three grammar concepts. Great work building real reading fluency in Gurmukhi!

objectives: Recall the definitions of noun, verb, and adjective, in Gurmukhi and English
Read a short passage built entirely from the week's vocabulary with correct comprehension
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Read the 3-sentence passage together, checking comprehension of each sentence.
3. Complete the cumulative review worksheet, mixing all 4 days' concepts.
4. Discuss any mismatches or uncertain answers together before finishing.
5. Celebrate finishing the first full week of this unit and reading a real passage independently.
differentiationTips: Struggling: read the passage together sentence by sentence, translating each before moving to the next
Ready for more: ask them to write one more sentence of their own using this week's vocabulary, following the noun+adjective+verb pattern
This is a good checkpoint to note which grammar concept (noun/verb/adjective) needs the most re-teaching before next week's unit
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. ਨਾਂਵ = noun. 2. ਕਿਰਿਆ = verb. 3. ਵਿਸ਼ੇਸ਼ਣ = adjective. Passage translation: 'This is a big house. The girl reads. The dog plays.'
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates the week's grammar-basics content (nouns/verbs/adjectives) and directly demonstrates reading fluency with an all-known-vocabulary passage, matching the course's own 'grammar basics ... and reading fluency' description.
